characteristic_lesions: osteosclerotic bone lesions (in contrast to lytic in MM)

biomarkers.name: Serum VEGF (markedly elevated)
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinctive marker; often markedly above normal. Response monitoring and supportive for diagnosis/prognosis

biomarkers.name: M-protein (typically IgA or IgG lambda light chain)
biomarkers.prevalence: Present in most cases; monoclonal plasma cell disorder is a mandatory major criterion
biomarkers.clinical_use: Lambda light chain restriction is characteristic

biomarkers.name: Osteosclerotic lesions on skeletal survey / CT
biomarkers.clinical_use: Distinguishing from MM (typically lytic); PET-CT can help detect lesions

biomarkers.name: HHV-8 (Castleman variant)
biomarkers.prevalence: Not a defining feature of POEMS; may be present in HHV-8-associated multicentric Castleman disease, which is considered distinct from classic POEMS
biomarkers.clinical_use: Helps distinguish HHV-8-associated multicentric Castleman disease from classic POEMS

biomarkers.name: Endocrine screening (thyroid, gonadal, adrenal, glucose)
biomarkers.clinical_use: One of the minor diagnostic criteria

histomorphological_subtype.primary_pattern: Small clonal plasma cell population in marrow producing IgA or IgG lambda M-protein; often with sclerotic bone lesions (in contrast to MM's typically lytic lesions)
histomorphological_subtype.grading: Not graded; VEGF level and organ involvement drive management

tumor_microenvironment.immune_context: VEGF elevation drives multiorgan syndrome — polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, skin changes; anti-VEGF therapy is not established standard treatment
tumor_microenvironment.stromal_features: Osteosclerotic bone lesions (unlike lytic MM); Castleman-like nodal architecture may be seen in Castleman disease-associated cases

cellular_states_and_lineage.cell_of_origin: Small clonal plasma cell population associated with VEGF overproduction driving multiorgan syndrome
cellular_states_and_lineage.differentiation_state: Terminal plasma cell differentiation with strong lambda light chain predominance; usually IgA or IgG subtype; often associated with sclerotic (not lytic) bone lesions
cellular_states_and_lineage.lineage_plasticity: Distinctive plasma cell biology — small clone associated with VEGF overproduction driving multiorgan syndrome; lambda light chain restriction is highly characteristic; overlap with Castleman disease-associated cases is recognized, while HHV-8-associated multicentric Castleman disease is considered a distinct entity
